direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is great, shot in the Academy format to look like a box CRT tube TV with glowing diodes that brings a nostalgia factor transporting you to 2006, generating solid suspense even if tonal issues hold it back from being the best; the direction on a microscale is good, bringing out the characters' motives and showing how chasing ratings and success affects each of them differently, particularly Chris Hansen as a narcissist who is obsessed with breaking the story and gaining fame rather than saving kids; the storytelling is a bit jumbled and held back by the writing, where Dan the decoy actor's arc as a hungry artist changed by the shoot works really well, but Hansen's storyline feels like a less nuanced hit piece and the third storyline with the producer could have been cut entirely; the issues with the storytelling very much show how this is the director's directorial debut; the tension is not built as well as it should have been for a suspense movie, largely because the tone feels like a mismatch and doesn't feel coherent

performance.comments: Carries the movie with his charismatic aura, playing the grittiness, narcissism, and ratings obsession very well, commanding every scene even though the material prevents him from going full-send into a Lou Bloom type character
Fine in the role of the producer, though the performance feels a little over-the-top at times
Delivers a good to very good performance showing the emotional toll on a naive, optimistic young actor whose morals become gradually corroded the deeper he gets into the show
Turns in a solid performance that fits well with the rest of the Perverted Justice crew
Does a decent, enjoyable job bringing comedic energy and eccentric quirks to his role as the head of Perverted Justice

cast.comments: A pretty good ensemble where everyone works well together and nobody gives a bad performance, with working chemistry and background decoys and predators that capture the amateurish feel of the real show

story.comments: The concept on paper is really good, following the rise and fall of To Catch a Predator and how Chris Hansen, the producer, and NBC chased ratings and were so obsessed with making great television that it made them sloppy, but in execution it fabricates and moves around storylines a decent amount and plays with the truth a little too much to fit the narrative, which hurts when making a hit piece showing the decay of journalistic ethics instead of relying on sound facts; the plot structure is the biggest issue with the movie because it runs too long at an hour and fifty minutes and feels uneven, starting when they are already famous rather than showing a full rise and fall, and it could have either cut out ten minutes of the producer storyline and early scenes to make it a tighter hour and forty minutes or redistributed that time to the fall, which feels very abrupt; the character writing is good and clearly establishes motives, showing how the chase for ratings and fame causes Chris Hansen to abandon journalistic ethics, while Dan's arc effectively captures an innocent, hungry actor whose morals become clouded by his involvement in the show, even if the producer's character writing feels like a slight mismatch

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is entertaining enough, but it is not as sharp or profound as it should be, feeling a little too goofy and dreamy rather than razor-sharp like Nightcrawler, contributing to the feeling of Nightcrawler on Xanax; the humor leans heavily into the absurdity of the dialogue from the real To Catch a Predator show, which had about a 33% hit rate for me, though the hit rate with the audience was not great as they were not really into it; the symbolism centers on the corrosion of journalistic ethics caused by an egotistical chase for ratings and media sensationalism, showing how that toxic obsession robs people of their innocence and corrupts their lives, from Hansen to the young decoy actor; the foreshadowing does a decent job telegraphing the inevitable downfall if you know the real-life story, illustrating how their escalating obsession and loss of ethics will lead directly to the final collapse

score.comments: Makes the film feel like a fairy tale alongside the warm cinematography, which creates a tonal mismatch for a suspense film, so I was not a huge fan of the score and felt it took away from the movie

soundtrack.comments: Very emblematic of the 2006 time period, featuring Fergie's 'London Bridge', songs from Rent, and an enjoyable Phoebe Bridgers end-credits song

cinematography.comments: Loved what they did here, shooting in the Academy format with the warm glow of CRT TV anode bulbs to create a dreamy, nostalgic 2006 look while delivering an intimate, gritty close-up character study of Chris Hansen's narcissistic obsession alongside authentic security-camera-style footage inspired by the original show

editing.comments: Works very well to capture a gritty surveillance state using multiple house angles while pacing the raw character study, though the frequent fades add to the dream state but can feel a bit corny at times

sound.comments: Crisp and well executed, incorporating authentic sounds emblematic of 2006 internet culture and early chat rooms

production_design.comments: Did a very good job of transporting you back to 2006, filled with period-accurate memorabilia and details like Fruit Roll-Ups and Rice Krispies Treats in vending machines, as well as capturing how NBC and ABC looked during that era

costumes.comments: Very emblematic of 2005 and 2006 clothing, doing a pretty decent job capturing the look of the era

review.pacing: Pretty slow and uneven, where the first hour has slower scenes that throw in a lot of plot not relevant to the main conflict, while the ending feels rushed like ten minutes when it should have been twenty or thirty, meaning it desperately needed ten minutes cut from the first half and either trimmed entirely or redistributed to flesh out the abrupt ending
review.climax: Not well executed at all, feeling like an abrupt, forced two-minute sequence that merges real events into a fictionalized ending that feels sensationalized itself, failing to stick the landing when the entire movie was supposed to build toward the fall and its consequences
review.tone: Stylistically inconsistent and tonally confused, failing to deliver the gritty, suspenseful thriller it aims to be by drifting into a lighter, fairy-tale dream state, ultimately feeling like Nightcrawler on Xanax instead of going full-send
review.final_notes: Saw at AMC Techridge after missing it at Fantastic Fest; it feels like society overhyped this movie because almost every screening was packed for a movie that doesn't match the quality everyone expected
review.overall: Overall, 'Primetime' is a good but not great movie that suffers from society overhyping it into what felt like it would be peak cinema; while I really enjoyed the 2006 nostalgia and Robert Pattinson carrying the film with his charisma as a character study of narcissistic ratings obsession, the film plays with the truth a little too much to fit the narrative when it was crucial to rely on sound facts for a movie about real people and journalistic ethics; it ultimately doesn't live up to the hype due to issues with story construction, slow pacing, tonal confusion that feels like Nightcrawler on Xanax, and an abrupt, loosely-true climax that fails to stick the landing
